size.note: Wikipedia gives 32–34 cm from bill to tail.

summary: A summer migrant to Europe and Asia that winters in Africa. The male is slate-grey, with the grey throat reaching well down the breast and a sharp line above the barred underparts. The iris, orbital ring, base of the bill and feet are yellow. Grey females have a buff background to the barring. Rufous-morph females have reddish-brown upper parts with dark bars. In flight it looks like a sparrowhawk. The male song is goo-ko. The female has a loud bubbling call. No Newman page was found. Months were left unset. The Kemp code NB was left unchanged.

similar.note: African Cuckoo has complete tail barring. Common Cuckoo has the outer tail feathers incompletely barred. Their upper tail coverts are both grey.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^11=2048 mature individuals (non-breeding visitor); paper interval half–double → 1024–4096.

sources.title: Kemp A.C., Herholdt J.J., Whyte I. & Harrison J. (2001). Birds of the two largest national parks in South Africa: a method to generate estimates of population size for all species and assess their conservation ecology. S. Afr. J. Sci. 97: 393–403.

head.pattern: The grey throat extends well down the breast.

underparts.pattern: Sharp demarcation from the grey breast to the barred underparts.

head.pattern: Grey morph. Pinkish-buff or buff on the neck sides and in the barring.

wings.pattern: Sometimes small rufous spots on the median and greater coverts and the outer webs of the secondaries.

upperparts.pattern: Rufous morph. Reddish-brown upper parts with dark grey or black bars. The black bars are narrower than the rufous bars.

wings.pattern: Dark bars, narrower than the rufous bars.

upperparts.pattern: Variable in the first autumn. Some are strongly barred chestnut-brown above, and others are plain grey.

wings.pattern: Whitish edges to the upper wing-coverts and primaries. Secondaries and greater coverts have chestnut bars or spots.

viewNotes.note: Slate-grey, with the grey breast ending sharply at the barred underparts.
Grey throat and breast, then barred underparts. The eye-ring and the base of the bill are yellow.
In flight it looks like a sparrowhawk, and the wingbeats are regular.
Barred underparts below a grey breast.

calls.description: The male song is goo-ko, usually from an open perch. The female has a loud bubbling call, which was not given a separate file. Grade A song from Västergötland. The filename is GokAmperna.mp3. Gok is the Swedish name on the file.
